instruction: Search only package names, not descriptions, for names matching the regular expression ^python3-.
context: apt-cache search PATTERN searches package metadata. --names-only restricts matching to package names instead of long descriptions; the pattern is a regular expression.

instruction: Recursively show dependencies of nginx, excluding Recommends relationships.
context: apt-cache depends PACKAGE displays dependency relationships. --recurse follows mentioned packages recursively, while --no-recommends suppresses Recommends relationships.

instruction: Prevent both linux-image-generic and linux-headers-generic from being automatically upgraded.
context: apt-mark hold marks each named package as held back, preventing automatic installation, upgrade, or removal.

instruction: Mark libfoo and libbar as automatically installed dependencies.
context: apt-mark auto marks every named package as automatically installed so it can be considered for automatic removal when no manual package depends on it.

instruction: Compute a 256-bit BLAKE2 digest of release.tar.zst and print it in BSD tag format.
context: b2sum --length=BITS selects a digest length in bits, and --tag emits BSD-style checksum output. The length must be a multiple of eight.

instruction: Verify checksums.b2, suppress successful OK lines, and do not fail for referenced files that are missing.
context: b2sum --check reads checksums from the named file. --quiet suppresses OK for successful files, and --ignore-missing does not fail or report status for missing files.

instruction: Encode token.bin with URL-safe Base64 and do not wrap the encoded output.
context: basenc --base64url selects the RFC 4648 URL-safe Base64 alphabet. --wrap=0 disables encoded-line wrapping.

instruction: Decode payload.b32 using the extended-hex Base32 alphabet while ignoring non-alphabet garbage bytes.
context: basenc --base32hex selects the extended-hex Base32 alphabet. --decode reverses encoding, and --ignore-garbage tolerates non-alphabet bytes in encoded input.

instruction: Show installed packages matching libssl* as one package name, a tab, and its version per line.
context: dpkg-query --show accepts package-name patterns. --showformat controls output; ${Package} and ${Version} expand fields, while \t and \n produce a tab and newline.

instruction: Using /mnt/sysroot as the package database root, list files owned by the bash package.
context: dpkg-query --root=DIRECTORY changes the filesystem and administrative database root. --listfiles PACKAGE lists files owned by that package.

instruction: Reflow only lines in notes.txt beginning with > to a maximum width of 60 columns, using uniform word and sentence spacing.
context: fmt --prefix=STRING reformats only lines beginning with that prefix and reattaches it. --width sets maximum line width; --uniform-spacing uses one space between words and two between sentences.

instruction: Preserve the first-two-line crown margin in letter.txt while splitting lines longer than 72 columns without refilling short lines.
context: fmt --crown-margin preserves indentation of a paragraph's first two lines. --split-only splits long lines without refilling, and --width=72 sets the maximum width.

instruction: Split server.log at every line beginning ERROR, omit each matching ERROR line, and name pieces error- followed by a three-digit number and .log.
context: csplit /REGEXP/ splits before a matching line and {*} repeats the prior pattern as many times as possible. --suppress-matched omits matched lines; --prefix and --suffix-format control output names.

instruction: Split book.txt before every line beginning CHAPTER, keep pieces if a later split errors, suppress byte-count output, and use chapter- plus three digits for names.
context: csplit /REGEXP/ splits before a matching line and {*} repeats that pattern. --keep-files retains outputs after an error, --quiet suppresses byte counts, and --prefix plus --digits control names.

instruction: Overwrite secret.key seven times, add a final zero-filled pass, then remove it using filename wiping.
context: shred --iterations=N selects overwrite passes. --zero adds a final zero pass, and --remove=wipe obfuscates the directory-entry name before unlinking it.

instruction: Force writing disk.img even if permissions need changing, overwrite exactly 10M without block-size rounding, and take random bytes from entropy.bin.
context: shred --force changes permissions if needed. --exact avoids rounding to a full block, --size=10M limits the overwritten size, and --random-source selects random input.

instruction: Choose at most five distinct numbers from the inclusive range 10 through 99, using seed.bin as the random-byte source.
context: shuf --input-range=LO-HI treats each integer in the inclusive range as an input line. --head-count limits output, and --random-source reads randomness from the named file. Without --repeat, output entries are distinct.

instruction: Randomly choose two of the literal inputs alpha, beta, and gamma and write the result directly to picks.txt.
context: shuf --echo treats each following argument as an input line. --head-count=2 limits output to two entries, and --output writes directly to the named file.

instruction: Convert every eligible run of spaces in aligned.txt to tabs using tab stops four columns apart.
context: unexpand converts spaces to tabs. --all converts all blanks rather than only initial blanks, and --tabs=4 places tab stops every four columns.

instruction: In table.txt, convert only leading blanks to tabs using explicit stops at columns 4 and 8, then every 4 columns afterward.
context: unexpand --first-only limits conversion to leading blanks. --tabs=4,8,/4 sets explicit stops at four and eight, then repeats every four columns after the last explicit stop.

instruction: Show device I/O error counters for /mnt/data as JSON and return failure if any counter is nonzero.
context: btrfs --format=json requests JSON when supported. device stats --check shows all device error counters and exits nonzero if any is nonzero.

instruction: Summarize only the total Btrfs disk usage of /mnt/data/snapshots using raw byte counts.
context: btrfs filesystem du --summarize emits only the total for each argument. --raw selects unscaled byte counts.

instruction: List only snapshots below /mnt/data and sort the results by path.
context: btrfs subvolume list -o filters below the supplied path, -s excludes ordinary subvolumes, and --sort=path orders by path.

instruction: Show detailed Btrfs scrub status for /mnt/data, including per-device statistics with raw byte values.
context: btrfs scrub status -d includes per-device statistics, -R prints raw statistics, and --raw avoids scaled byte units.

instruction: List only acquired unique names on the system bus without headers, footers, or a pager.
context: busctl --system selects the system bus. --unique and --acquired restrict names; --no-legend and --no-pager remove presentation wrappers.

instruction: List object paths, rather than a tree drawing, for org.freedesktop.Notifications on the user bus without truncating them.
context: busctl --user selects the user bus. --list makes tree output a plain object-path list, and --full disables ellipsizing.

instruction: Read the ActiveState property from org.freedesktop.systemd1 unit ssh.service on the system bus and return short JSON.
context: busctl get-property takes service, object, interface, then property. --system selects the system bus and --json=short requests compact JSON.

instruction: On the system bus, call Reload on systemd's Manager, refuse service auto-start, and wait at most 5 seconds.
context: busctl call takes service, object, interface, and method. --auto-start=no refuses activation and --timeout=5 bounds reply waiting.

instruction: List the filesystem contents of app_1.2_amd64.deb with verbose detail.
context: dpkg-deb --contents lists archive filesystem members; --verbose enables detailed output.

instruction: Print only the Package, Version, and Architecture control fields from app.deb.
context: dpkg-deb --field DEB FIELD... prints only the requested control fields in the supplied order.

instruction: Show app.deb as package name, a tab, version, and newline using an explicit format.
context: dpkg-deb --show displays archive information. --showformat expands package fields and the requested tab and newline escapes.

instruction: Extract both filesystem files and control metadata from app.deb into staging/ with verbose output.
context: dpkg-deb --raw-extract places filesystem content and DEBIAN control metadata in the destination; --verbose reports details.

instruction: Set PID 4242 to best-effort I/O scheduling class with priority level 3.
context: ionice class 2 is best-effort; --classdata sets its priority and --pid selects the process.

instruction: Put every process in process group 900 into the idle I/O scheduling class and ignore a failure to apply it.
context: ionice class 3 is idle, --pgid targets a process group, and --ignore continues if the requested setting cannot be applied.

instruction: Assign processes owned by UID 1001 to real-time I/O class at priority 6.
context: ionice class 1 is real-time; --classdata selects its priority and --uid targets processes belonging to the UID.

instruction: Run ./backup with --incremental in the idle I/O scheduling class, ignoring failure to set the class.
context: With a command operand, ionice launches that command under the requested class. --ignore tolerates inability to set scheduling.

instruction: Silently test whether /srv/data itself is a mount point without following a final symlink.
context: mountpoint --quiet suppresses output. --nofollow checks the named final path rather than following a symlink.

instruction: Print the major:minor device number of the filesystem containing /srv/data without following a final symlink.
context: mountpoint --fs-devno prints the filesystem device number as major:minor; --nofollow preserves final-symlink identity.

instruction: Print the major:minor device number for block device /dev/nvme0n1p2.
context: mountpoint --devno prints the major:minor number of the named block device.

instruction: Print only the major device number of the filesystem containing /mnt/backup.
context: mountpoint --fs-devno emits major:minor. cut uses colon as delimiter and selects field one, leaving only the major number.

instruction: Run ./worker as both user and group svc, initialize svc's supplementary groups, and prohibit gaining new privileges.
context: setpriv --reuid and --regid set real and effective IDs. --init-groups initializes supplementary groups and --no-new-privs blocks privilege gains.

instruction: Run /usr/bin/id as nobody:nogroup with no supplementary groups and a reset environment.
context: setpriv changes real and effective user and group IDs. --clear-groups removes supplementary groups and --reset-env initializes a clean login-like environment.

instruction: Run ./sandbox after removing net_raw and sys_admin from the capability bounding set and prohibiting new privileges.
context: setpriv --bounding-set with minus-prefixed capability names removes them. --no-new-privs disallows later privilege gains.

instruction: Run ./child with TERM as its parent-death signal, keep current supplementary groups, and set effective UID to 1001.
context: setpriv --pdeathsig sets the signal delivered when the parent dies. --keep-groups retains supplementary groups and --euid sets effective UID.

instruction: Run /usr/local/bin/report as transient unit nightly-report.service in batch.slice with a 512M memory maximum and wait for completion.
context: systemd-run --unit names the transient unit, --slice assigns it, --property sets a unit property, and --wait waits for termination.

instruction: In the user manager, run ./build once from /srv/project with MODE=release and collect the unit afterward.
context: systemd-run --user selects the user manager. --working-directory and --setenv configure execution; --collect unloads the unit after it finishes.

instruction: Schedule /usr/local/sbin/cleanup to run 15 minutes from now as cleanup-once.service without blocking for startup.
context: systemd-run --on-active schedules a transient timer relative to activation. --unit names it and --no-block returns without waiting for startup.

instruction: Run make -j4 in a transient scope with nice level 10 and pass its standard streams directly through.
context: systemd-run --scope creates a transient scope. --nice sets scheduling niceness and --pipe directly connects standard input, output, and error.

instruction: Show only the Leader and State property values for container web01, with no pager.
context: machinectl show accepts repeated --property filters. --value omits property names and --no-pager writes directly.

instruction: Run /usr/bin/id inside container web01 as user deploy with LANG=C and without paging.
context: machinectl shell invokes a command in a container. --uid selects the user, --setenv adds an environment variable, and --no-pager disables paging.

instruction: Copy config.yaml from the host to /etc/app/config.yaml in web01 and create the destination directory if it is missing.
context: machinectl copy-to copies a host path into a container. --mkdir creates a missing destination directory before copying.

instruction: Show web01 status without a pager, including its last 25 journal lines in short-precise format.
context: machinectl status can include journal output. --lines bounds entries, --output selects journal format, and --no-pager writes directly.

instruction: Show status for all links as compact JSON with no pager.
context: networkctl --all includes every link, --json=short emits compact JSON, and --no-pager disables paging.

instruction: Show full, unellipsized status and detailed statistics for interface eth0 without a pager.
context: networkctl status accepts a link pattern. --stats adds detailed statistics, --full prevents ellipsizing, and --no-pager disables paging.

instruction: Show LLDP neighbors for eth0 as pretty JSON without headers or a pager.
context: networkctl lldp lists neighbors for selected devices. --json=pretty formats JSON, --no-legend removes headers, and --no-pager disables paging.

instruction: Edit the 50-debug.conf drop-in for eth0 without reloading networkd or udev afterward.
context: networkctl edit modifies configuration for a device. --drop-in names the drop-in and --no-reload suppresses automatic daemon reloads.

instruction: Run make test in a recorded terminal, write output to test.typescript, flush after every write, and return make's exit status.
context: script --command runs a fixed command, --return propagates its status, --flush writes promptly, and the operand names the output log.

instruction: Record both input and output in session.io, timing in session.time, force advanced logging format, and suppress startup messages.
context: script --log-io records both streams, --log-timing records timing, --logging-format=advanced selects the compatible format, and --quiet suppresses messages.

instruction: Append a terminal session to audit.log, never echo input, and allow the output file even if it is a link.
context: script --append preserves an existing log, --echo=never disables input echo, and --force permits a linked output file.

instruction: Run ./chatty under terminal recording, stop when logs exceed 10M, save stdout in chatty.out, and return the child status.
context: script --command runs the child, --output-limit terminates on excess output, --log-out names the stdout log, and --return propagates child status.

instruction: Compute a transition from the current SELinux context using type httpd_t, then run ./serve on port 8080.
context: runcon --compute derives a transition context from the current context; --type selects its type, followed by the command and arguments.

instruction: Compute an SELinux transition as user staff_u, role staff_r, and type staff_t before running /usr/bin/id.
context: With --compute, runcon combines supplied user, role, and type components with the current context before executing the command.

instruction: Compute a transition with role sysadm_r and MLS range s0-s0:c0.c3, then run ./audit with --once.
context: runcon --compute derives a context while --role and --range override those SELinux components; remaining words form the command.

instruction: Run /usr/bin/true under the exact SELinux context system_u:system_r:backup_t:s0.
context: Without --compute, runcon takes one complete SELinux CONTEXT operand followed by COMMAND and its arguments.

instruction: Inspect every component of /srv/app/config.yaml in long format and include SELinux security contexts.
context: namei --long includes modes, owners, groups, and vertical alignment. --context additionally prints each component's security context.

instruction: Inspect /var/lib/app/current without following symlinks, showing modes and marking mount-point directories.
context: namei --nosymlinks avoids following links, --modes displays mode bits, and --mountpoints marks mount-point directories.

instruction: Inspect both /etc/hosts and /etc/resolv.conf, showing owner and group names in vertically aligned output.
context: namei accepts multiple pathnames. --owners shows owner and group names, while --vertical vertically aligns output columns.

instruction: Show a long component listing for /opt/releases/latest/bin/app but do not follow symbolic links.
context: namei --long combines modes, owners, and aligned display. --nosymlinks stops symlink resolution.

instruction: Enter every namespace of PID 4321, preserve current credentials, inherit that process's environment, and run /usr/bin/id.
context: nsenter --target selects the process, --all enters all namespaces, --preserve-credentials retains IDs, and --env inherits target environment.

instruction: Enter PID 4321's network and UTS namespaces, change to /srv/app, and run ./healthcheck --once.
context: nsenter --net and --uts enter the target's network and hostname namespaces. --wd changes working directory before the command.

instruction: Enter PID 4321's user and mount namespaces, use its root directory, set UID and GID to 1000, then run /usr/bin/id.
context: nsenter selects target namespaces, --root uses the target root, and --setuid plus --setgid choose credentials after entry.

instruction: Enter PID 4321's PID and cgroup namespaces without forking before executing ps -ef.
context: nsenter --pid and --cgroup enter those target namespaces. --no-fork executes the supplied program directly.

instruction: Create user, PID, and mount namespaces mapped to root, fork, mount a fresh /proc, and run zsh -f.
context: unshare --map-root-user creates a user namespace, --pid and --mount create namespaces, --fork is required for PID isolation, and --mount-proc mounts procfs.

instruction: Create new network and UTS namespaces, fork, and run hostname isolated-host.
context: unshare --net and --uts isolate networking and hostname state. --fork runs the supplied hostname command in a child.

instruction: Map the current user into a new user namespace, create a mount namespace with private propagation, change to /tmp/work, and run ./task.
context: unshare --map-current-user creates a user mapping, --mount creates a mount namespace, --propagation controls it, and --wd changes directory.

instruction: Create a PID namespace, fork sleep 600, and send TERM to that child if unshare exits.
context: unshare --pid isolates process IDs; --fork creates the namespace child and --kill-child=TERM arranges cleanup when unshare dies.

instruction: Set PID 4242's soft open-file limit to 1024 and hard limit to 4096, showing verbose results.
context: prlimit --pid targets a process; --nofile=SOFT:HARD changes open-file limits and --verbose reports details.

instruction: Run ./worker with core dumps disabled and a 16M soft and 32M hard stack limit.
context: With a command, prlimit applies resource limits before execution. --core and --stack accept SOFT:HARD pairs.

instruction: Show PID 4242's limits as raw RESOURCE, SOFT, HARD, and UNITS columns without headings.
context: prlimit --output selects columns. --raw removes formatting and --noheadings suppresses the header row.

instruction: Run ./job with a 60-second soft and 90-second hard CPU limit and at most 32 processes for both limits.
context: prlimit --cpu sets CPU seconds and --nproc sets process count; each accepts a soft:hard pair before COMMAND.

instruction: Preallocate 2GiB starting 1GiB into cache.bin while keeping its apparent size unchanged, with verbose output.
context: fallocate --offset and --length select the range. --keep-size preserves apparent size and --verbose reports the operation.

instruction: Punch a 64MiB hole starting 128MiB into disk.img without changing its apparent size.
context: fallocate --punch-hole deallocates the selected range and implies keep-size; --offset and --length locate it.

instruction: Zero and allocate exactly 8MiB beginning 4MiB into image.raw, preserving its apparent size.
context: fallocate --zero-range zeros and allocates a range. --offset and --length select it, while --keep-size preserves file size.

instruction: Remove a 1MiB range starting 16MiB into data.bin and shift all later data toward the beginning.
context: fallocate --collapse-range removes the byte range and shifts following data left; --offset and --length define it.

instruction: Attach disk.img to the first free loop device read-only, scan its partition table, and print the chosen device.
context: losetup --find selects an unused device, --show prints it, --read-only prevents writes, and --partscan creates partition devices.

instruction: Attach payload.img at offset 1MiB with a 512MiB size limit and 4096-byte logical sectors, printing the selected free loop device.
context: losetup --offset and --sizelimit expose a file range, --sector-size sets logical sectors, and --find --show selects and prints a device.

instruction: List loop devices associated with disk.img as JSON, including only NAME, OFFSET, SIZELIMIT, and RO columns.
context: losetup --associated filters by backing file. --list enables tabular selection, --json changes format, and --output selects columns.

instruction: Attach disk.img using direct I/O, refuse overlapping loop mappings, and print the chosen free device.
context: losetup --nooverlap avoids conflicting mappings, --direct-io=on requests O_DIRECT, and --find --show selects and prints a free device.

instruction: Resolve filesystem label BACKUP to its device path while bypassing the blkid cache.
context: blkid --label resolves a label to a device name. --cache-file=/dev/null bypasses the normal cache.

instruction: Low-level probe /dev/loop0 starting 1MiB in, limit probing to 64MiB, and print only TYPE and UUID values.
context: blkid --probe bypasses cache. --offset and --size bound probing, repeated --match-tag selects tags, and --output=value omits labels.

instruction: Probe /dev/sdb1 without cache, restrict results to filesystem usage, and emit export-style key-value output.
context: blkid --cache-file=/dev/null bypasses cache, --usages filters usage classes, and --output=export emits key-value lines.

instruction: Find only the first device with UUID 1111-2222 and output just the device name.
context: blkid --match-token filters by NAME=value, --list-one stops at the first match, and --output=device prints only its device name.

instruction: List network namespaces as JSON with only NS, PID, USER, and COMMAND columns, without truncating text.
context: lsns --type filters namespace type, --json selects JSON, --output selects columns, and --notruncate preserves text.

instruction: Show PID namespaces as a tree in raw format without headings, including NS, PID, PPID, and COMMAND.
context: lsns --type=pid filters namespaces, --tree arranges hierarchy, --raw removes formatting, --noheadings removes headers, and --output selects columns.

instruction: Show the mount namespace containing PID 4242 in list format with all available columns.
context: lsns --task selects namespaces containing a PID, --type=mnt filters mount namespaces, --list selects list output, and --output-all includes all columns.

instruction: List user namespaces without multiline wrapping, using only NS, UID, USER, NPROCS, and PATH columns.
context: lsns --type=user filters user namespaces, --nowrap keeps each record on one line, and --output selects columns.

instruction: Run /bin/sh in a new PID namespace with /usr read-only at /usr, an empty /tmp, procfs at /proc, and working directory /tmp.
context: bwrap --unshare-pid isolates PIDs, --ro-bind maps a read-only tree, --tmpfs and --proc create filesystems, and --chdir sets working directory.

instruction: Unshare all supported namespaces but retain networking, clear the environment, set HOME to /tmp/home, and run /usr/bin/env.
context: bwrap --unshare-all isolates supported namespaces, --share-net retains networking, --clearenv removes variables, and --setenv adds one.

instruction: Create UTS and network namespaces, set hostname sandbox, start a new terminal session, kill the child if its parent dies, and run /bin/zsh -f.
context: bwrap unshares UTS and network state, --hostname sets the isolated hostname, --new-session creates a session, and --die-with-parent cleans up.

instruction: Create a user namespace as UID and GID 1000, mount a private device filesystem at /dev, bind app read-only at /app, and run /app/start.
context: bwrap --unshare-user enables custom --uid and --gid. --dev creates a private device filesystem and --ro-bind maps app read-only.

instruction: Print PATH and HOME as NUL-terminated values, then convert those record terminators to newlines.
context: printenv --null terminates each requested variable value with NUL. tr maps each NUL byte to a newline, so pipeline framing remains compatible.

instruction: Extract parent directories of /srv/z/file and /opt/a/file as NUL-delimited records and sort them without changing the delimiter.
context: dirname --zero emits a NUL after each parent path. sort --zero-terminated consumes and emits the same record framing.

instruction: For /var/log/zeta.log and /tmp/alpha.log, remove directories and the .log suffix, emit NUL-delimited names, and sort with NUL framing.
context: basename --multiple handles both paths, --suffix removes .log, and --zero emits NUL records. sort --zero-terminated preserves that framing.

instruction: List all configuration variables applicable to /srv/app and sort the colon-separated output by variable name.
context: getconf -a PATH lists all variables including path-dependent values. sort uses colon as field separator and key 1,1 to order by variable name.
